mcqs.question: A student pushes a stationary box with a constant horizontal force of 20 N but the box does not move. Which statement correctly describes the work done by the student on the box?

options.A: The student does 20 N·m of work because a force is applied.
options.B: No work is done because there is no displacement.
options.C: Work is done only if the box eventually moves, regardless of the force.
options.D: Work is done because the student’s muscles expend energy.

mcqs.answer: No work is done because there is no displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as W = F × s × cosθ. If the displacement (s) is zero, the product is zero, so no work is done regardless of the magnitude of the force. Option A ignores the displacement term, C misstates the condition, and D confuses internal energy expenditure with mechanical work on the box.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: A force of 15 N acts on a crate that moves 4 m horizontally. Which condition must be satisfied for the force to do positive work on the crate?

options.A: The force must be perpendicular to the direction of motion.
options.B: The force must have a component in the same direction as the displacement.
options.C: The crate must be lifted vertically.
options.D: The force must be applied for at least 10 seconds.

mcqs.answer: The force must have a component in the same direction as the displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Work = F·s = Fs cosθ. Positive work requires cosθ > 0, meaning the force has a component along the displacement. Option A gives zero work (cos 90° = 0). Option C is irrelevant to horizontal motion, and D concerns time, which does not appear in the work formula.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question:
Two situations are considered:
1. A force of 10 N pushes an object 5 m in the same direction as the force.
2. A force of 20 N pushes the same object 2 m opposite to the direction of the force.
Which situation results in a greater magnitude of work done on the object?

options.C: Both situations give the same magnitude of work.
options.D: Neither situation does any work because the forces are not constant.

mcqs.explanation: Work = F·s·cosθ. In situation 1, θ = 0°, so work = 10 × 5 × 1 = 50 J (positive). In situation 2, θ = 180°, so work = 20 × 2 × (‑1) = –40 J; the magnitude is 40 J, which is less than 50 J. Option B ignores the sign, C is false, and D is incorrect because the forces are constant and displacement occurs.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the SI unit of work, the joule, is correct?

options.A: 1 joule equals 1 newton multiplied by 1 meter.
options.B: 1 joule equals 1 kilogram multiplied by 1 meter per second squared.
options.C: 1 joule equals 1 newton divided by 1 meter.
options.D: 1 joule equals 1 watt divided by 1 second.

mcqs.answer: 1 joule equals 1 newton multiplied by 1 meter.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, 1 J = 1 N·m (force times displacement). Option B describes a newton (kg·m/s²) not a joule. Option C would give units of N/m, which is not energy. Option D incorrectly uses division; the correct relation is 1 J = 1 W·s, not W/ s.
